<cite ref="Bava Batra 8a:6">B. Bath. 8ᵃ</cite> <he>רמי כ׳ חדתא וכ׳</he> (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 80) put on orphans (heirs) the obligation of contributing towards a new ditch.

<cite ref="Bava Batra 8a:7">Ib.</cite> (<cite ref="E00513"><he>הכל</he></cite>) <he>לכ׳</he> (<cite ref="D00000"><he>ד</he></cite>)<he>פתיא וכ׳</he> (Ms. F. <cite ref="B00700"><he>בֵּירָא</he></cite>, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note) even scholars must lend their services in digging a street-well; <cite ref="Bava Metzia 108a">B. Mets. 108ᵃ</cite> (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 60).
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 110a:8">Ib. 110ᵃ</cite> <he>וכרי כ׳</he> and must do what digging may be required (ditch, well), v. <cite ref="I00593"><he>טַסְקָא</he></cite>.
Ib. לכ׳ דנהרא for dredging the river (or channel).—*בית כ׳ House of Heaps (Ruins), a cacophemistic change of the name בֵּית גַּלְיָא, v. גַּלְיָא II.
Ab. Zar. 46ᵃ; Tem. 28ᵇ (Var. כַּלְיָיא destruction).—[V., however, גַּדָּא a. גַּלָּא.]—
